# 1. Introduction

This analysis examines the comparison of six-degrees-of-freedom (6DoF) audio rendering algorithms for immersive classical music experiences. The study is part of a doctoral dissertation on "Spatial audio for networked music performances" (Gdańsk University of Technology, 2022).

## 1.1 Experiment Context

**Audio material:** Aria of Donna Elvira from the opera *Don Giovanni* by W. A. Mozart (15-second looped excerpt). The soprano soloist was the localization target, with the accompanying orchestra present in the sound scene.

**Virtual sound scene:** 27 third-order Ambisonics (3OA) spheres with interpolated region between microphones 5, 6, and 10. An additional ambisonic sphere was rendered at the center for the single-sphere renderers (ScnRot and Com.BinVR).

**Equipment:** Oculus Quest 2 head-mounted display with 6DoF tracking (yaw, pitch, roll + sway, surge, heave). A custom MaxMSP signal processing engine interfaced HMD tracking data to the audio renderers.

**Visual scene:** Minimal VR environment with wooden floor (0.5m grid spacing), sky-like ceiling, and yellow center marker—no visual objects to avoid localization bias.

## 1.2 Rendering Algorithms Compared

| Abbreviation | Full Name | Description |
|--------------|-----------|-------------|
| **ScnRot** | IEM SceneRotator | 3DoF baseline from IEM plug-in suite |
| **Com.BinVR** | COMPASS BinauralVR | Single HOA sphere with spatial parametric decomposition and spatial warping |
| **Com.6DoF** | COMPASS 6DoF | Multiple HOA spheres with beamformer-driven decomposition |
| **Zyl.6DoF** | Zylia 6DoF HOA Renderer | Loudness crossfading interpolation method |
| **Del.wgts** | Delaunay weights | Simple weighting using Delaunay triangulation and barycentric coordinates |

## 1.3 Test Procedure

**Localization task:**

- Participants indicated perceived azimuth of the soprano soloist
- Only horizontal component measured
- Participants returned to center (yellow square) before each assessment
- Unlimited exploration time; only last assessment recorded

**Quality rating task (MUSHRA-like):**

- 101-point scale (0-100)
- Rating bins: 0-20 Bad, 20-40 Poor, 40-60 Fair, 60-80 Good, 80-100 Excellent
- Participants could compare cases in any order and revise answers

## 1.4 Participants

**36** participants tested (27 PG, 9 ZL); 35 analyzed for localization, 34 for ratings. Participants were:

- Academic staff of Multimedia Systems Department, Gdańsk University of Technology
- Members of Academic Choir of Gdańsk University of Technology
- Staff of Zylia sp. z o.o. (second site)
- Audio industry professionals

All had at least amateur music education or were audio professionals.

## 1.5 Dependent Variables

1. **Localization Error** (objective): Angular error in azimuth (degrees) from ground truth (312°)
2. **Quality Rating** (subjective): MUSHRA-like scale (0-100)

# 2. Setup and Data Loading

## 2.1 Required Packages

library(tidyverse)

## 2.2 Load Raw Data from CSV Files

```{r load_raw_data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, collapse=TRUE, comment=''}
# Define data directory
data_dir <- "../data"

# Get all localization and MUSHRA files (excluding discarded)
loc_files <- list.files(data_dir, pattern = "^(PG|ZL)-[0-9]+-.*-Localization\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
mus_files <- list.files(data_dir, pattern = "^(PG|ZL)-[0-9]+-.*-MUSHRA\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)

cat("Found", length(loc_files), "localization files\n")
cat("Found", length(mus_files), "MUSHRA files\n")

# Function to parse filename and read data
read_participant_data <- function(filepath, type = "localization") {
  # Extract info from filename
  filename <- basename(filepath)
  parts <- str_match(filename, "^(PG|ZL)-(\\d+[a-z]?)-(\\d+)-")

  location <- parts[2]
  subject_id <- parts[3]
  timestamp <- parts[4]
  
  # Read the file (semicolon separated). Files from the two sites use different
  # decimal marks (PG: comma, ZL: period); detect per file, because readr treats
  # "." as a grouping mark under decimal_mark = ","
  dec <- if (any(grepl(",", readLines(filepath, warn = FALSE)[-1]))) "," else "."
  df <- read_delim(filepath, delim = ";", locale = locale(decimal_mark = dec),
                   show_col_types = FALSE)
  
  # Ensure numeric columns are numeric (fixes type conflicts during bind_rows)
  if (type == "localization" && "Elevation" %in% names(df)) {
    df$Elevation <- as.numeric(df$Elevation)
  }
  if ("Azimuth" %in% names(df)) {
    df$Azimuth <- as.numeric(df$Azimuth)
  }
  
  # Add metadata
  df$Location <- location
  df$SubjectID <- paste0(location, "-", subject_id)
  df$Timestamp <- timestamp
  
  return(df)
}

# Load all localization data
df_loc_raw <- map_dfr(loc_files, ~read_participant_data(.x, "localization"))

# Load all MUSHRA (rating) data
df_rat_raw <- map_dfr(mus_files, ~read_participant_data(.x, "rating"))

# Preview
cat("\nLocalization data dimensions:", dim(df_loc_raw), "\n")
cat("Rating data dimensions:", dim(df_rat_raw), "\n")
```

## 2.3 Data Preprocessing

```{r preprocess_data, collapse=TRUE, comment=''}
# Algorithm name mapping (raw -> analysis names)
# Verified against original experiment design
algorithm_map <- c(
  "Reference" = "ScnRot",      # IEM SceneRotator (3DoF baseline)
  "Sparta" = "Com.6DoF",       # COMPASS 6DoF (multiple HOA spheres)
  "Sparta3DoF" = "Com.BinVR",  # COMPASS BinauralVR (single HOA sphere)
  "Zylia1" = "Zyl.6DoF",       # Zylia 6DoF HOA Renderer
  "Zylia2" = "Del.wgts"        # Delaunay triangulation with barycentric weights
)

# Mapping verified against the final Max patch (route Sparta Zylia1 Zylia2 Reference Sparta3DoF)

# Process Localization data
df_loc <- df_loc_raw %>%
  mutate(
    Algorithm = dplyr::recode(AlgorithmName, !!!algorithm_map),
    Algorithm = factor(Algorithm, levels = c("ScnRot", "Com.BinVR", "Com.6DoF", "Zyl.6DoF", "Del.wgts")),
    SubjectID = factor(SubjectID),
    # Ground truth azimuth of the soprano soloist (experiment design)
    GroundTruth = 312,
    # Calculate localization error (circular distance)
    Response = (Azimuth + AzimuthRef) %% 360,  # Combine to get absolute response
    Error = abs((Response - GroundTruth + 180) %% 360 - 180),  # Circular difference
    Log.Error = log(Error + 0.1)  # Add small constant to handle zeros
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Algorithm)) %>%
  dplyr::select(SubjectID, Location, Timestamp, SongID, Algorithm, Azimuth, Elevation,
         AzimuthRef, Response, GroundTruth, Error, Log.Error)

# Process Rating data  
df_rat <- df_rat_raw %>%
  mutate(
    Algorithm = dplyr::recode(AlgorithmName, !!!algorithm_map),
    Algorithm = factor(Algorithm, levels = c("ScnRot", "Com.BinVR", "Com.6DoF", "Zyl.6DoF", "Del.wgts")),
    SubjectID = factor(SubjectID),
    Rating = as.numeric(Score)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Algorithm)) %>%
  dplyr::select(SubjectID, Location, Timestamp, SongID, Algorithm, Rating)

# Summary
cat("Processed localization data:", nrow(df_loc), "observations\n")
cat("Processed rating data:", nrow(df_rat), "observations\n")
cat("Number of subjects (loc):", n_distinct(df_loc$SubjectID), "\n")
cat("Number of subjects (rat):", n_distinct(df_rat$SubjectID), "\n")
```

## 3.3 Participant Performance Screening

Before proceeding with the main analysis, we should identify participants who may not have understood the localization task or whose performance was consistently poor across all conditions.

```{r participant_screening, collapse=TRUE, comment=''}
# Calculate participant-level statistics
participant_performance <- df_loc %>%
  group_by(SubjectID) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Error = mean(Error, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Error = median(Error, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Error = sd(Error, na.rm = TRUE),
    Min_Error = min(Error, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max_Error = max(Error, na.rm = TRUE),
    N_Trials = n(),
    N_Large_Errors = sum(Error > 50),  # Count errors > 50°
    Prop_Large_Errors = N_Large_Errors / N_Trials,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Mean_Error))

# Display top 10 worst performers
kable(head(participant_performance, 10), digits = 2,
      caption = "Top 10 Participants with Highest Mean Localization Error") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

# Visualize participant performance distribution
ggplot(participant_performance, aes(x = reorder(SubjectID, Mean_Error), y = Mean_Error)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "#2E86AB", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 30, linetype = "dashed", color = "orange", size = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 45, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 5, y = 32, label = "30° threshold", color = "orange", size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = 5, y = 47, label = "45° threshold", color = "red", size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Mean Localization Error by Participant",
       subtitle = "Ordered from worst to best performance",
       x = "Participant", y = "Mean Error (degrees)") +
  theme_pubclean() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 6),
        legend.position = "none")

ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "03a_participant_screening.png"), 
       width = 14, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

### Proposed Exclusion Criteria

We propose three possible exclusion criteria:

1. **Conservative (Mean > 45°)**: Exclude participants with mean error > 45° across all trials
2. **Moderate (Mean > 30°)**: Exclude participants with mean error > 30°
3. **Strict (>80% large errors)**: Exclude if >80% of trials have error > 50°

```{r exclusion_criteria, collapse=TRUE, comment=''}
# Define thresholds
threshold_conservative <- 45
threshold_moderate <- 30
threshold_strict_prop <- 0.80
threshold_strict_error <- 50

# Apply criteria
excluded_conservative <- participant_performance %>%
  filter(Mean_Error > threshold_conservative) %>%
  mutate(Criterion = "Conservative: Mean > 45°")

excluded_moderate <- participant_performance %>%
  filter(Mean_Error > threshold_moderate) %>%
  mutate(Criterion = "Moderate: Mean > 30°")

excluded_strict <- participant_performance %>%
  filter(Prop_Large_Errors > threshold_strict_prop) %>%
  mutate(Criterion = "Strict: >80% trials with error > 50°")

# Summary table
exclusion_summary <- data.frame(
  Criterion = c("Conservative (Mean > 45°)", 
                "Moderate (Mean > 30°)", 
                "Strict (>80% trials > 50°)"),
  N_Excluded = c(nrow(excluded_conservative), 
                 nrow(excluded_moderate), 
                 nrow(excluded_strict)),
  N_Remaining = c(n_distinct(df_loc$SubjectID) - nrow(excluded_conservative),
                  n_distinct(df_loc$SubjectID) - nrow(excluded_moderate),
                  n_distinct(df_loc$SubjectID) - nrow(excluded_strict)),
  Prop_Excluded = c(nrow(excluded_conservative) / n_distinct(df_loc$SubjectID),
                    nrow(excluded_moderate) / n_distinct(df_loc$SubjectID),
                    nrow(excluded_strict) / n_distinct(df_loc$SubjectID))
)

kable(exclusion_summary, digits = 3,
      caption = "Comparison of Exclusion Criteria") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

# Show which participants would be excluded under each criterion
cat("\n### Conservative Criterion (Mean > 45°):\n")
if (nrow(excluded_conservative) > 0) {
  print(excluded_conservative %>% 
          dplyr::select(SubjectID, Mean_Error, Median_Error,
                        N_Large_Errors, Prop_Large_Errors) %>%
          arrange(desc(Mean_Error)))
} else {
  cat("No participants excluded.\n")
}

cat("\n### Moderate Criterion (Mean > 30°):\n")
if (nrow(excluded_moderate) > 0) {
  print(excluded_moderate %>% 
          dplyr::select(SubjectID, Mean_Error, Median_Error,
                        N_Large_Errors, Prop_Large_Errors) %>%
          arrange(desc(Mean_Error)))
} else {
  cat("No participants excluded.\n")
}

cat("\n### Strict Criterion (>80% trials > 50°):\n")
if (nrow(excluded_strict) > 0) {
  print(excluded_strict %>% 
          dplyr::select(SubjectID, Mean_Error, Median_Error,
                        N_Large_Errors, Prop_Large_Errors) %>%
          arrange(desc(Mean_Error)))
} else {
  cat("No participants excluded.\n")
}
```

### Recommended Approach

Based on standard practices in spatial audio research and the distribution of errors:

- **Recommendation**: Use **Conservative criterion (Mean > 45°)** or investigate individual 
  cases manually
- **Rationale**: 
  - Localization in complex acoustic scenes with multiple sources is inherently difficult
  - 30° may be too strict given the complexity of the task (soprano + orchestra)
  - 45° represents ~1/8 of the full circle, a reasonable threshold for "complete confusion"
  - Manual inspection allows checking if poor performers show consistent patterns vs. random responding

```{r apply_exclusion, collapse=TRUE, comment=''}
# For this analysis, we'll use the CONSERVATIVE criterion (Mean > 45°)
# Store original data
df_loc_original <- df_loc
df_rat_original <- df_rat
n_subjects_original <- n_distinct(df_loc$SubjectID)

# Apply exclusion (if any participants meet criterion)
if (nrow(excluded_conservative) > 0) {
  excluded_ids <- excluded_conservative$SubjectID
  df_loc <- df_loc %>% filter(!SubjectID %in% excluded_ids)
  df_rat <- df_rat %>% filter(!SubjectID %in% excluded_ids)
  
  cat("\n### Exclusion Applied\n")
  cat("Original N =", n_subjects_original, "\n")
  cat("Excluded N =", length(excluded_ids), "(", paste(excluded_ids, collapse = ", "), ")\n")
  cat("Final N =", n_distinct(df_loc$SubjectID), "\n")
} else {
  cat("\n### No Exclusions Applied\n")
  cat("All", n_subjects_original, "participants meet the quality criterion (Mean Error < 45°)\n")
}

# Keep ratings only from participants who passed localization screening
df_rat <- df_rat %>% filter(SubjectID %in% unique(df_loc$SubjectID))

# Drop unused factor levels after exclusion
df_loc$SubjectID <- droplevels(df_loc$SubjectID)
df_loc$Algorithm <- droplevels(df_loc$Algorithm)

df_rat$SubjectID <- droplevels(df_rat$SubjectID)
df_rat$Algorithm <- droplevels(df_rat$Algorithm)

# Check factor levels remain valid for modeling
cat("\n### Post-exclusion factor levels:\n")
cat("Algorithms:", nlevels(df_loc$Algorithm), "levels -",
    paste(levels(df_loc$Algorithm), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Subjects:", nlevels(df_loc$SubjectID), "participants\n")

# Verify we still have sufficient data structure for mixed models
if (nlevels(df_loc$Algorithm) < 2) {
  stop("ERROR: Less than 2 algorithm levels remaining after exclusion. Cannot proceed with analysis.")
}
if (nlevels(df_loc$SubjectID) < 10) {
  warning("WARNING: Less than 10 subjects remaining. Mixed model estimates may be unstable.")
}
```

# 4. Assumption Checks

## 4.1 Normality of Localization Error

The localization error data is expected to follow a log-normal distribution (error data is typically right-skewed and bounded at zero).

```{r normality_loc, collapse=TRUE, comment=''}
# Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests for log-normality
ks_results_loc <- df_loc %>%
  group_by(Algorithm) %>%
  summarise(
    fit_meanlog = tryCatch(
      fitdistr(Error + 0.1, "lognormal")$estimate["meanlog"],
      error = function(e) NA
    ),
    fit_sdlog = tryCatch(
      fitdistr(Error + 0.1, "lognormal")$estimate["sdlog"],
      error = function(e) NA
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Perform KS tests
ks_tests <- df_loc %>%
  group_by(Algorithm) %>%
  summarise(
    ks_stat = tryCatch({
      fit <- fitdistr(Error + 0.1, "lognormal")$estimate
      ks.test(Error + 0.1, "plnorm", meanlog = fit[1], sdlog = fit[2])$statistic
    }, error = function(e) NA),
    ks_pvalue = tryCatch({
      fit <- fitdistr(Error + 0.1, "lognormal")$estimate
      ks.test(Error + 0.1, "plnorm", meanlog = fit[1], sdlog = fit[2])$p.value
    }, error = function(e) NA),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(LogNormal = ifelse(ks_pvalue > 0.05, "Yes", "No"))

kable(ks_tests, digits = 3,
      caption = "Kolmogorov-Smirnov Tests for Log-Normality of Localization Error",
      col.names = c("Algorithm", "D statistic", "p-value", "Log-Normal?")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

# 5. Statistical Analysis: Mixed Models

## 5.1 Analysis of Localization Error (Gamma GLMM)

### 5.1.1 Model Justification

Localization error is a positive, right-skewed continuous variable bounded at zero. A **Gamma Generalized Linear Mixed Model (GLMM)** is theoretically optimal for such data because:

1. Gamma distribution naturally models positive continuous data with right skew
2. No need for log transformation - the link function handles the relationship
3. Variance increases with the mean (heteroscedasticity is built into the model)
4. More appropriate than log-normal LMM when residual normality is violated

```{r glmm_loc_build, collapse=TRUE, comment=''}
# Set contrasts for Algorithm (treatment coding with ScnRot as reference)
df_loc$Algorithm <- relevel(df_loc$Algorithm, ref = "ScnRot")

# Add small constant to handle any zeros (if present)
df_loc$Error_pos <- df_loc$Error + 0.1

# Gamma GLMM with log link (standard for Gamma)
# Random intercept for subjects
glmm_loc <- glmmTMB(Error_pos ~ Algorithm + (1 | SubjectID),
                    data = df_loc,
                    family = Gamma(link = "log"))

cat("Gamma GLMM Model Summary:\n\n")
summary(glmm_loc)
```

### 5.1.2 Model Comparison

```{r glmm_loc_comparison, collapse=TRUE, comment=''}
# Compare with simpler models
# Null model (no algorithm effect)
glmm_loc_null <- glmmTMB(Error_pos ~ 1 + (1 | SubjectID),
                         data = df_loc,
                         family = Gamma(link = "log"))

# Likelihood ratio test
cat("Likelihood Ratio Test: Algorithm Effect\n\n")
lr_test <- anova(glmm_loc_null, glmm_loc)
print(lr_test)

cat("\nAIC Comparison:\n")
cat("  Null model (no Algorithm):", AIC(glmm_loc_null), "\n")
cat("  Full model (with Algorithm):", AIC(glmm_loc), "\n")
cat("  Difference:", AIC(glmm_loc_null) - AIC(glmm_loc), 
    "(positive = full model better)\n")
```

### 5.1.3 Residual Diagnostics (DHARMa)

DHARMa provides proper residual diagnostics for GLMMs by creating scaled residuals
through simulation.

```{r glmm_loc_dharma, fig.height=6}
# Create DHARMa residuals (scaled residuals via simulation)
set.seed(42)  # For reproducibility
dharma_loc <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = glmm_loc, n = 1000)

# Plot DHARMa diagnostics
plot(dharma_loc, main = "DHARMa Residual Diagnostics - Localization Error")

# Save the plot
png(file.path(plot_dir, "06_dharma_diagnostics_localization.png"), 
    width = 10, height = 6, units = "in", res = 300)
plot(dharma_loc)
dev.off()

# Formal tests
cat("\nDHARMa Residual Tests:\n\n")

# Uniformity test (KS test on scaled residuals - should be uniform if model is correct)
uniformity_test <- testUniformity(dharma_loc, plot = FALSE)
cat("1. Uniformity Test (KS):\n")
cat("   D =", round(uniformity_test$statistic, 4), 
    ", p =", round(uniformity_test$p.value, 4), "\n")
cat("   Interpretation:", 
    ifelse(uniformity_test$p.value > 0.05, 
           "Residuals are uniform (model fits well)\n",
           "Some deviation from uniformity detected\n"))

# Dispersion test
dispersion_test <- testDispersion(dharma_loc, plot = FALSE)
cat("\n2. Dispersion Test:\n")
cat("   Dispersion ratio =", round(dispersion_test$statistic, 4), 
    ", p =", round(dispersion_test$p.value, 4), "\n")
cat("   Interpretation:", 
    ifelse(dispersion_test$p.value > 0.05, 
           "No over/underdispersion detected\n",
           ifelse(dispersion_test$statistic > 1, 
                  "Overdispersion detected\n", 
                  "Underdispersion detected\n")))

# Outlier test
outlier_test <- testOutliers(dharma_loc, plot = FALSE)
cat("\n3. Outlier Test:\n")
cat("   p =", round(outlier_test$p.value, 4), "\n")
cat("   Interpretation:", 
    ifelse(outlier_test$p.value > 0.05, 
           "No significant outliers\n",
           "Significant outliers detected\n"))

# Store test results for export
dharma_uniformity_p <- uniformity_test$p.value
dharma_dispersion_p <- dispersion_test$p.value
dharma_dispersion_ratio <- dispersion_test$statistic
```

### 5.1.4 Additional Diagnostic Plots

```{r glmm_loc_residuals, fig.height=5}
# Extract residuals for custom plots
resid_loc <- data.frame(
  Fitted = fitted(glmm_loc),
  Residuals = residuals(glmm_loc, type = "pearson"),
  ScaledResiduals = dharma_loc$scaledResiduals,
  Algorithm = df_loc$Algorithm,
  SubjectID = df_loc$SubjectID
)

# Residuals by Algorithm
g1 <- ggplot(resid_loc, aes(x = Algorithm, y = Residuals)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Pearson Residuals by Algorithm",
       x = "Algorithm", y = "Pearson Residuals") +
  theme_pubclean()

# Scaled residuals by Algorithm (should be uniform 0-1)
g2 <- ggplot(resid_loc, aes(x = Algorithm, y = ScaledResiduals)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightgreen", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  labs(title = "DHARMa Scaled Residuals by Algorithm",
       subtitle = "Should be uniform (0-1) if model is correct",
       x = "Algorithm", y = "Scaled Residuals") +
  theme_pubclean()

# Random effects check
ranef_loc <- ranef(glmm_loc)$cond$SubjectID
ranef_df <- data.frame(
  SubjectID = rownames(ranef_loc),
  Intercept = ranef_loc[,1]
)

g3 <- ggplot(ranef_df, aes(sample = Intercept)) +
  geom_qq() +
  geom_qq_line(color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Q-Q Plot of Random Effects",
       x = "Theoretical Quantiles", y = "Random Intercepts") +
  theme_pubclean()

p_resid_loc <- grid.arrange(g1, g2, g3, ncol = 3)
ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "06b_residual_diagnostics_localization.png"), p_resid_loc, 
       width = 15, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

### 5.1.5 Type II Wald Chi-Square Test

```{r glmm_loc_anova, collapse=TRUE, comment=''}
# For GLMMs, we use Type II Wald chi-square tests
cat("Type II Wald Chi-Square Tests (Analysis of Deviance)\n\n")
anova_loc <- car::Anova(glmm_loc, type = "II")
print(anova_loc)

# Effect size: Calculate pseudo R-squared (Nakagawa & Schielzeth)
# Using variance components
var_fixed <- var(predict(glmm_loc, re.form = NA))  # Fixed effects variance
var_random <- as.numeric(VarCorr(glmm_loc)$cond$SubjectID)  # Random intercept variance
# For Gamma with log link, residual variance approximation
var_residual <- trigamma(1/sigma(glmm_loc)^2)  # Based on Gamma distribution property

R2_marginal <- var_fixed / (var_fixed + var_random + var_residual)
R2_conditional <- (var_fixed + var_random) / (var_fixed + var_random + var_residual)

cat("\nPseudo R-squared (Nakagawa & Schielzeth method):\n")
cat("  Marginal R² (fixed effects only):", round(R2_marginal, 3), "\n")
cat("  Conditional R² (fixed + random):", round(R2_conditional, 3), "\n")

# Store for export
chisq_loc <- anova_loc$Chisq[1]
df_loc_anova <- anova_loc$Df[1]
p_loc_anova <- anova_loc$`Pr(>Chisq)`[1]
```

### 5.1.6 Post-hoc Pairwise Comparisons

```{r glmm_loc_posthoc, collapse=TRUE, comment=''}
# Post-hoc pairwise comparisons with Holm correction
# emmeans works with glmmTMB
emm_loc <- emmeans(glmm_loc, ~ Algorithm, type = "response")
pairs_loc <- pairs(emm_loc, adjust = "holm")

cat("Pairwise Comparisons (Holm-adjusted):\n")
cat("Note: Ratios are shown because of log link (ratio > 1 means first > second)\n\n")
print(pairs_loc)

# Also show as summary table
pairs_df <- as.data.frame(pairs_loc)
pairs_df$significant <- ifelse(pairs_df$p.value < 0.05, "*", "")
pairs_df$significant[pairs_df$p.value < 0.01] <- "**"
pairs_df$significant[pairs_df$p.value < 0.001] <- "***"

kable(pairs_df, digits = 4,
      caption = "Post-hoc Pairwise Comparisons: Localization Error (Ratios)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

### 5.1.7 Estimated Marginal Means

```{r glmm_loc_emmeans, collapse=TRUE, comment=''}
# Get EMMs on response scale (back-transformed)
emm_loc_df <- as.data.frame(emm_loc)

# Check column names - glmmTMB uses asymp.LCL and asymp.UCL
# Adjust for the +0.1 offset we added
emm_loc_df$Error_mean <- emm_loc_df$response - 0.1
emm_loc_df$Error_lower <- emm_loc_df$asymp.LCL - 0.1
emm_loc_df$Error_upper <- emm_loc_df$asymp.UCL - 0.1

# Rename for clarity (these are model-estimated means on original scale)
kable(emm_loc_df[, c("Algorithm", "response", "SE", "Error_mean", "Error_lower", "Error_upper")], 
      digits = 2,
      col.names = c("Algorithm", "EMM (+0.1)", "SE", "Estimated Mean (°)", "Lower 95% CI", "Upper 95% CI"),
      caption = "Estimated Marginal Means: Localization Error (Gamma GLMM)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

# Also compute ICC for random effects
var_subj <- as.numeric(VarCorr(glmm_loc)$cond$SubjectID)
# For Gamma, total variance approximation
icc_loc <- var_subj / (var_subj + var_residual)
cat("\nIntraclass Correlation (ICC) for Subject:", round(icc_loc, 3), "\n")
cat("Interpretation:", round(icc_loc * 100, 1), "% of variance is between subjects\n")
```

## 5.2 Analysis of Quality Ratings

### 5.2.1 Model Building

```{r lmm_rat_build, collapse=TRUE, comment=''}
# Set contrasts
df_rat$Algorithm <- relevel(df_rat$Algorithm, ref = "ScnRot")
contrasts(df_rat$Algorithm) <- contr.treatment(nlevels(df_rat$Algorithm))

# Model 1.0: Basic model with random intercept for subjects
m1.0.rat <- lme(Rating ~ Algorithm, 
                random = ~ 1 | SubjectID, 
                data = df_rat, 
                method = "REML")

# Model 1.1: Heterogeneous residual variance across algorithms
m1.1.rat <- update(m1.0.rat, weights = varIdent(form = ~ 1 | Algorithm))

# Compare models
cat("Model Comparison: Homogeneous vs Heterogeneous Variance\n")
print(anova(m1.1.rat, m1.0.rat))
```

### 5.2.4 Formal Residual Tests

```{r lmm_rat_formal_diagnostics, collapse=TRUE, comment=''}
# Shapiro-Wilk test on model residuals
residuals_rat <- resid(selected_model_rat, type = "pearson")
sw_resid_rat <- shapiro.test(residuals_rat)

cat("Shapiro-Wilk Test on Model Residuals (Rating):\n")
cat("  W =", round(sw_resid_rat$statistic, 4), 
    ", p =", round(sw_resid_rat$p.value, 4), "\n")
cat("  Interpretation:", 
    ifelse(sw_resid_rat$p.value > 0.05, 
           "Residuals appear normally distributed (p > .05)\n",
           "Some deviation from normality detected; LMM is robust to moderate violations\n"))

# Levene's test for homogeneity of variance across algorithms
cat("\nLevene's Test for Homogeneity of Variance (Rating):\n")
levene_rat <- leveneTest(Rating ~ Algorithm, data = df_rat, center = median)
print(levene_rat)
levene_rat_p <- levene_rat$`Pr(>F)`[1]
cat("  Interpretation:", 
    ifelse(levene_rat_p > 0.05, 
           "Variance is homogeneous across groups (p > .05)\n",
           "Heterogeneous variance detected; consider using varIdent() in nlme\n"))

# Influential observations check
std_resid_rat <- residuals_rat / sd(residuals_rat)
n_extreme_rat <- sum(abs(std_resid_rat) > 3)
cat("\nInfluential Observations Check:\n")
cat("  Observations with |standardized residual| > 3:", n_extreme_rat, 
    "out of", length(std_resid_rat), "\n")
cat("  Percentage:", round(100 * n_extreme_rat / length(std_resid_rat), 1), "%\n")
```

### 5.2.5 ANOVA and Post-hoc Tests

```{r lmm_rat_anova, collapse=TRUE, comment=''}
cat("F-test (anova.lme; single fixed factor, so sequential = marginal)\n\n")
anova_rat <- anova(selected_model_rat)
print(anova_rat)

# Effect size
F_val <- anova_rat$`F-value`[2]
df1 <- anova_rat$numDF[2]
df2 <- anova_rat$denDF[2]
eta_sq <- (F_val * df1) / (F_val * df1 + df2)
cat("\nApproximate η² for Algorithm effect:", round(eta_sq, 3), "\n")
```

## 7.2 Export Results for LaTeX

## Sensitivity analyses

Site effect, and robustness of the pairwise results when the author's own session (PG-004) or the second site (ZL) is excluded.

```{r sensitivity, collapse=TRUE, comment=''}
# Participants tested: everyone with at least one valid (non-discarded) run
n_tested    <- n_distinct(c(df_loc_raw$SubjectID, df_rat_raw$SubjectID))
ids_tested  <- unique(c(as.character(df_loc_raw$SubjectID), as.character(df_rat_raw$SubjectID)))
n_tested_pg <- sum(startsWith(ids_tested, "PG-"))
n_tested_zl <- sum(startsWith(ids_tested, "ZL-"))

# Site as a fixed effect (likelihood-ratio tests, ML)
site_loc_m0 <- glmmTMB(Error_pos ~ Algorithm + (1 | SubjectID), data = df_loc, family = Gamma(link = "log"))
site_loc_m1 <- glmmTMB(Error_pos ~ Algorithm + Location + (1 | SubjectID), data = df_loc, family = Gamma(link = "log"))
site_loc <- anova(site_loc_m0, site_loc_m1)
site_rat_m0 <- lme(Rating ~ Algorithm, random = ~ 1 | SubjectID, data = df_rat, method = "ML")
site_rat_m1 <- lme(Rating ~ Algorithm + Location, random = ~ 1 | SubjectID, data = df_rat, method = "ML")
site_rat <- anova(site_rat_m0, site_rat_m1)
site_loc_chisq <- site_loc$Chisq[2]; site_loc_p <- site_loc$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]
site_rat_chisq <- site_rat$L.Ratio[2]; site_rat_p <- site_rat$`p-value`[2]

# Refit the main models on a subset and collect Holm-adjusted pairwise results
fit_subset <- function(keep) {
  dl <- droplevels(df_loc[keep(df_loc$SubjectID), ])
  dr <- droplevels(df_rat[keep(df_rat$SubjectID), ])
  gl <- glmmTMB(Error_pos ~ Algorithm + (1 | SubjectID), data = dl, family = Gamma(link = "log"))
  lr <- lme(Rating ~ Algorithm, random = ~ 1 | SubjectID, data = dr, method = "REML")
  pl <- as.data.frame(summary(pairs(emmeans(gl, ~ Algorithm, type = "response"), adjust = "holm")))
  pr <- as.data.frame(summary(pairs(emmeans(lr, ~ Algorithm), adjust = "holm")))
  list(n_loc = n_distinct(dl$SubjectID), n_rat = n_distinct(dr$SubjectID),
       chisq = car::Anova(gl, type = "II")$Chisq[1], p_loc = car::Anova(gl, type = "II")$`Pr(>Chisq)`[1],
       F = anova(lr)$`F-value`[2], p_rat = anova(lr)$`p-value`[2], pl = pl, pr = pr,
       sig_loc = sort(as.character(pl$contrast[pl$p.value < 0.05])),
       sig_rat = sort(as.character(pr$contrast[pr$p.value < 0.05])))
}
pair_p <- function(tab, a, b) {
  hit <- grepl(a, tab$contrast, fixed = TRUE) & grepl(b, tab$contrast, fixed = TRUE)
  stopifnot(sum(hit) == 1)
  tab$p.value[hit]
}
sens_full     <- fit_subset(function(id) rep(TRUE, length(id)))
sens_noauthor <- fit_subset(function(id) id != "PG-004")
sens_nosite2  <- fit_subset(function(id) !startsWith(as.character(id), "ZL-"))
same_set_nosite2 <- identical(sens_full$sig_loc, sens_nosite2$sig_loc) && identical(sens_full$sig_rat, sens_nosite2$sig_rat)

cat("Tested:", n_tested, "(PG", n_tested_pg, ", ZL", n_tested_zl, ")\n")
cat("Site LRT, localization: chisq =", round(site_loc_chisq, 2), ", p =", round(site_loc_p, 3), "\n")
cat("Site LRT, ratings: L.Ratio =", round(site_rat_chisq, 2), ", p =", round(site_rat_p, 3), "\n")
for (s in list(list("all", sens_full), list("without PG-004", sens_noauthor), list("without ZL", sens_nosite2))) {
  cat("\n", s[[1]], ": N loc", s[[2]]$n_loc, ", N rat", s[[2]]$n_rat,
      "\n  significant localization pairs:", paste(s[[2]]$sig_loc, collapse = "; "),
      "\n  significant rating pairs:", paste(s[[2]]$sig_rat, collapse = "; "), "\n")
}
cat("\nSame significant pairs without ZL:", same_set_nosite2, "\n")

write.csv(rat_summary, file.path(results_dir, "descriptive_rating.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# 2. ANOVA/Model comparison results
# For localization: Gamma GLMM uses chi-square test
# For ratings: LMM uses F-test
anova_results <- data.frame(
  DV = c("Localization_Error_GammaGLMM", "Quality_Rating_LMM"),
  Effect = "Algorithm",
  Test_Statistic = c(chisq_loc, anova_rat$`F-value`[2]),
  Test_Type = c("Chi-square", "F"),
  df1 = c(df_loc_anova, anova_rat$numDF[2]),
  df2 = c(NA, anova_rat$denDF[2]),  # Chi-square doesn't have df2
  p_value = c(p_loc_anova, anova_rat$`p-value`[2]),
  R2_marginal = c(R2_marginal, NA),
  R2_conditional = c(R2_conditional, NA),
  eta_sq_approx = c(
    NA,  # Not applicable for GLMM
    (anova_rat$`F-value`[2] * anova_rat$numDF[2]) / 
      (anova_rat$`F-value`[2] * anova_rat$numDF[2] + anova_rat$denDF[2])
  )
)
write.csv(anova_results, file.path(results_dir, "anova_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

  cat("\\newcommand{\\pairLocStar", k, "}{", stars(pairs_loc_df$p.value[i]), "}\n", sep = "")
}
for (i in seq_len(nrow(pairs_rat_df))) {
  k <- gsub("6DoF", "SixDoF", gsub("\\.", "", gsub(" - ", "Vs", pairs_rat_df$contrast[i])))
  cat("\\newcommand{\\pairRatStar", k, "}{", stars(pairs_rat_df$p.value[i]), "}\n", sep = "")
}

sink()

cat("Results exported to:", results_dir, "\n")
cat("Files created:\n")
list.files(results_dir)
```

## 7.3 Dynamic Interpretation

The following interpretation is generated dynamically based on the actual analysis results:

```{r dynamic_interpretation, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# Determine which algorithm had lowest localization error
best_loc_alg <- emm_loc_df$Algorithm[which.min(emm_loc_df$Error_mean)]
worst_loc_alg <- emm_loc_df$Algorithm[which.max(emm_loc_df$Error_mean)]

# Determine which algorithm had highest quality rating
best_rat_alg <- emm_rat_df$Algorithm[which.max(emm_rat_df$emmean)]
worst_rat_alg <- emm_rat_df$Algorithm[which.min(emm_rat_df$emmean)]

# Count significant post-hoc comparisons
sig_loc <- sum(pairs_df$p.value < 0.05)
sig_rat <- sum(pairs_df_rat$p.value < 0.05)

cat("### Localization Error (Gamma GLMM)\n\n")

if (p_loc_anova < 0.05) {
  cat("- **Significant effect of Algorithm** detected: χ²(", 
      df_loc_anova, ") = ", round(chisq_loc, 2), ", *p* ", 
      ifelse(p_loc_anova < 0.001, "< .001", 
             paste0("= ", round(p_loc_anova, 3))),
      "\n", sep = "")
  cat("- Pseudo R² (marginal): ", round(R2_marginal, 3), 
      "; Pseudo R² (conditional): ", round(R2_conditional, 3), "\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("- **No significant effect of Algorithm** detected: χ²(", 
      df_loc_anova, ") = ", round(chisq_loc, 2), ", *p* = ", 
      round(p_loc_anova, 3), "\n", sep = "")
}

cat("- Best performer: **", as.character(best_loc_alg), 
    "** (estimated mean = ", round(min(emm_loc_df$Error_mean), 2), "°)\n", sep = "")
cat("- Worst performer: **", as.character(worst_loc_alg), 
    "** (estimated mean = ", round(max(emm_loc_df$Error_mean), 2), "°)\n", sep = "")
cat("- Number of significant pairwise differences: ", sig_loc, " out of 10\n\n", sep = "")

cat("### Quality Rating (LMM)\n\n")

if (anova_rat$`p-value`[2] < 0.05) {
  cat("- **Significant effect of Algorithm** detected: *F*(", 
      anova_rat$numDF[2], ", ", anova_rat$denDF[2], ") = ", 
      round(anova_rat$`F-value`[2], 2), ", *p* ", 
      ifelse(anova_rat$`p-value`[2] < 0.001, "< .001", 
             paste0("= ", round(anova_rat$`p-value`[2], 3))),
      ", η² ≈ ", round(anova_results$eta_sq_approx[2], 3), "\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("- **No significant effect of Algorithm** detected: *F*(", 
      anova_rat$numDF[2], ", ", anova_rat$denDF[2], ") = ", 
      round(anova_rat$`F-value`[2], 2), ", *p* = ", 
      round(anova_rat$`p-value`[2], 3), "\n", sep = "")
}

cat("- Highest rated: **", as.character(best_rat_alg), 
    "** (M = ", round(max(emm_rat_df$emmean), 1), ")\n", sep = "")
cat("- Lowest rated: **", as.character(worst_rat_alg), 
    "** (M = ", round(min(emm_rat_df$emmean), 1), ")\n", sep = "")
cat("- Number of significant pairwise differences: ", sig_rat, " out of 10\n\n", sep = "")

cat("### Correlation Between Measures\n\n")

if (cor_test$p.value < 0.05) {
  direction <- ifelse(cor_test$estimate > 0, "positive", "negative")
  strength <- ifelse(abs(cor_test$estimate) < 0.3, "weak",
                     ifelse(abs(cor_test$estimate) < 0.5, "moderate", "strong"))
  cat("- **Significant ", strength, " ", direction, " correlation** between localization error and quality rating: ",
      "*r* = ", round(cor_test$estimate, 3), ", *p* ", 
      ifelse(cor_test$p.value < 0.001, "< .001", paste0("= ", round(cor_test$p.value, 3))), "\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("- **No significant correlation** between localization error and quality rating: ",
      "*r* = ", round(cor_test$estimate, 3), ", *p* = ", round(cor_test$p.value, 3), "\n", sep = "")
}

cat("\n### Model Quality Indicators\n\n")
cat("- **Localization (Gamma GLMM)**: ICC = ", round(icc_loc, 3), 
    "; Marginal R² = ", round(R2_marginal, 3), 
    "; Conditional R² = ", round(R2_conditional, 3), "\n", sep = "")
cat("- **Rating (LMM)**: ICC = ", round(model_summary_rat$ICC, 3), 
    " (", round(model_summary_rat$ICC * 100, 1), "% of variance due to between-subject differences)\n", sep = "")
```

## 7.4 Limitations and Considerations

```{r limitations, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat("**Note:** The following are considerations for publication:\n\n")

cat("1. **Sample size**: N = ", n_distinct(df_loc$SubjectID), 
    " participants. For mixed models, this is ", 
    ifelse(n_distinct(df_loc$SubjectID) >= 30, "adequate", "borderline"),
    " for detecting medium effect sizes.\n\n", sep = "")

cat("2. **Localization model**: Gamma GLMM was used instead of log-normal LMM because ",
    "localization error is positive, right-skewed, and bounded at zero. The Gamma ",
    "distribution naturally handles these properties. Marginal R² = ", 
    round(R2_marginal, 3), " indicates the fixed effect explains ",
    round(R2_marginal * 100, 1), "% of variance.\n\n", sep = "")

cat("3. **Rating model effect size**: η² ≈ ", round(anova_results$eta_sq_approx[2], 3), 
    " indicates a ", 
    ifelse(anova_results$eta_sq_approx[2] < 0.06, "small", 
           ifelse(anova_results$eta_sq_approx[2] < 0.14, "medium", "large")),
    " effect size for quality ratings.\n\n", sep = "")

cat("4. **Multiple comparisons**: Holm correction applied to ", 
    nrow(pairs_df), " pairwise comparisons per DV.\n\n", sep = "")

# Model diagnostics
cat("5. **Localization model diagnostics (DHARMa)**:\n")
cat("   - Uniformity test: p = ", round(dharma_uniformity_p, 3), 
    ifelse(dharma_uniformity_p > 0.05, " (model fits well)", " (some misfit)"), "\n", sep = "")
cat("   - Dispersion: ratio = ", round(dharma_dispersion_ratio, 3), ", p = ", 
    round(dharma_dispersion_p, 3),
    ifelse(dharma_dispersion_p > 0.05, " (no over/underdispersion)", 
           ifelse(dharma_dispersion_ratio > 1, " (overdispersion)", " (underdispersion)")), "\n\n", sep = "")

cat("6. **Rating model diagnostics**: Shapiro-Wilk on residuals: W = ", 
    round(sw_resid_rat$statistic, 4), ", p = ", round(sw_resid_rat$p.value, 3),
    ifelse(sw_resid_rat$p.value > 0.05, " (normality assumption met)", 
           " (some deviation)"),
    "; Levene's test: p = ", round(levene_rat_p, 3),
    ifelse(levene_rat_p > 0.05, " (homogeneity met)", " (heterogeneity)"), "\n\n", sep = "")
```
